title: Micro-OKR trajectory checklist and weekly swing notes
content:
Context and intent:
- This is my working checklist for micro-OKRs (2–4 week cycles) + weekly swing notes. Not polished; mostly prompts-to-self, small experiments, and quick data checks.

Top-level goal (quarter rolling): Improve inference economics while keeping p99 latency under 75ms for small chat workloads.
Primary metrics I watch:
- p99 latency (client-observed): baseline 72ms (last 2w), target <= 65ms by end of Q1
- cost/1k tokens (hosted): baseline $0.78, target -10% via batching/quantization
- ERR (end-to-end reliability rate): 99.6% -> target 99.9%

This week (spr-week 5, 2026-03-08 -> 2026-03-14):
- Monday quick sync w/ Jonas: agreed to trial aggressive micro-batching on dev pool (config MB-3). Notes: watch tail latency spike on 1.5s windows.
- Tuesday: ran A/B (MB-3 vs MB-1) on a 10k request slice: MB-3 reduced avg cost by ~7.4% but p99 bumped by ~6ms on long prompts. Need to isolate causality (KV sharding?).
- Wed: small rollback to MB-2 for canary on prod-dedicated. Observed subtle queue buildup during spiky load (Slack thread: CD8F2JG4D).
- Thu: patched retry backoff in client SDK (PR #987). Start collecting retry-attempt distribution.
- Fri: retro notes + plan for next week.

Signals / quick observations:
- Batching gives >5% cost wins commonly, but tail latency sensitive to request size distribution.
- Quantized 4-bit variant shows small perf regression on long sequences (more memory thrash?) — need kernel tracing.
- KV cache hit rate improved after lowering TTL to 20s for streaming sessions (from 45s) — odd but consistent on small-chat traces.

Open questions (to answer before next check-in):
- Is the p99 uptick purely queuing or kernel-level slowdown? (Action: Jonas to add perf counters; I will add queue-length metric to dashboard)
- How much additional cost do retries add at 99th percentile? (Action: parse retry logs, map to token slices)
- Can we safely auto-switch to MB-3 only when median request size < X tokens? (Action: write routing rule prototype)

Mini experiments to run (priority order):
1) MB-conditional-routing prototype (2d) — if median payload < 512 tokens, route to MB-3. Fallback: MB-1.
2) Kernel trace on quantized model with seq>1k (collect 200 traces).
3) Retry cost attribution: join retry logs w/ token counts and cost table.

Quick tasks / TODOs (this doc is my inbox):
- [ ] Draft short note for TLHs: "batching guardrails" (short bullets) — due Mon 2026-03-16
- [ ] Update candid dashboard: add queue-length per-pool, retry-rate heatmap — assigned to me, due Wed 2026-03-18
- [ ] Post preliminary MB-conditional experiment plan in #serving-runtime channel
- [x] Patch client retry backoff (PR merged Thu)

Retrospective (what went well / what to change):
- Wins: small wins from MB-2 rollout; better visibility after adding retry telemetry. Good cross-team response time from infra.
- Pain: rolled MB-3 too quickly on larger slices — should have gated on median token size. Need safer canary gating.
- Personal: felt reactive mid-week; want to batch decisions into two weekly windows (Mon planning + Thu review).

Personal rating / focus (scale 1-5):
- Focus: 3.5 -> want to reduce context switching; set up more automation for metric alerts.
- Impact: 4 -> experiments are moving needle, but still noisy.

Next-week plan (concrete):
- Monday: finalize MB-conditional rule and run synthetic load test (goal: keep p99 delta < 3ms while getting >=6% cost reduction).
- Mid-week: run kernel traces; sync with Research on quantized exec path.
- End-week: compile findings into short 1-pager for product-hosted-api review (include cost projection table and gating checklist).

Notes to self (random):
- Remember to include user-visible SLA implications when proposing any routing rules (product will ask).
- Keep PR descriptions concise: "what broke, why this mitigates, rollback steps."
- If MB-conditional is messy, fallback to simpler TTL tuning and smaller batch size increments.

Links and refs (working):
- Perf ticket RED-2147 (queue-length spikes)
- MB experiment slice: RED-3112 (analytics)
- PR #987 (client retry backoff)

End of file — quick coffee break reminder: 10–12min.
